item.title: [7] Coexisting magnetic, charge, and superconducting orders in the two-dimensional Hubbard model
item.description:
Last authors: Walter Metzner, Demetrio Vilardi

Authors: Robin Scholle, Pietro M. Bonetti, Walter Metzner, Demetrio Vilardi

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant theory for competing orders in unconventional superconductors.

Tags: #superconduct #Hubbard #theory

Abstract: The authors analyze here the competition and coexistence of magnetic, charge, and d -wave superconducting orders in the two-dimensional Hubbard model using renormalization-group-improved Hartree–Fock calculations. The resulting phase diagram reveals superconductivity coexisting with Néel order on the electron-doped side and with spiral or stripe order on the hole-doped side. In the stripe phase, the superconducting gap is spatially modulated together with the charge order.

item.title: [7] Bridging the gap between numerics and experiment in freestanding graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Christopher Winterowd, Fakher Assaad

Authors: Maksim Ulybyshev, Savvas Zafeiropoulos, Christopher Winterowd, Fakher Assaad

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Connects QMC numerics to experimental graphene observables.

Tags: #graphene #theory #method

Abstract: Here, the authors revisit the question of the logarithmic renormalization of the Fermi velocity in graphene. Using large-scale Quantum Monte Carlo simulations of lattices with up to 2 × 10 4 interacting electrons, they directly connect experimental data with unbiased, nonperturbative calculations starting from a microscopic Hamiltonian. Their results reveal that even random-phase approximation corrections are quantitatively insufficient at realistic interaction strengths for suspended graphene, while continuum perturbation theory misses important lattice-scale effects. Remarkably, the optical conductivity still remains constant pointing to exact cancellation of different corrections.

item.title: [8] NMR evidence of pairing fluctuations above Tc and absence of spin magnetism in the time-reversal symmetry-breaking state of Ba1−xKxFe2As2
item.description:
Last authors: Hannes Kühne, Vadim Grinenko

Authors: Florian Bärtl, Nadia Stegani, Federico Caglieris, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important spectroscopic study on iron-based superconductors with relevant TRSB physics.

Tags: #superconductivity #NMR #iron-pnictide

Abstract: Four- or higher-order fermionic condensates can form in non-BCS multicomponent superconductors. Here, the authors present spectroscopic evidence for pairing correlations that appear well above the superconducting critical temperature in the highly overdoped Ba 1 − x K x Fe 2 As 2 system with broken time-reversal symmetry (BTRS). The NMR and μ SR findings show that multicomponent superconductivity appears homogeneously throughout the entire sample volume and that the BTRS state is unrelated to conventional spin magnetism.

item.description:

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of an altermagnet, highly relevant to topological/magnetic materials interest.

Tags: #altermagnet #transport #Fermisurface

Abstract: The authors present here results from electrical magnetotransport measurements on microstructures of altermagnetic CrSb in pulsed fields up to 68 T. They study the temperature and field-orientation dependence of magnetic quantum oscillations in combination with first-principles calculations. The observed frequency spectrum agrees well with density functional theory calculations that take spin-orbit coupling into account, without invoking significant a d h o c band shifts. The findings validate the predicted electronic band structure of CrSb hosting multiple semimetallic bands and a locally alternating spin polarization.
